key_insight: Brain-Adapter uses a dual-stream, text-guided MIL framework to classify acute intracranial findings on 3D CT scans without needing dense manual annotations.
clinical_relevance: It could make brain CT triage and reporting more scalable by leveraging both raw radiology text and scan-level visual signals to improve multi-label diagnosis.
method: Text-Conditioned Attention uses diagnostic sentences as queries to match image regions with disease concepts.
A parallel visual MIL stream learns global scan features using structured labels extracted by an LLM.
An uncertainty-aware refinement module fuses both streams at inference and improves ambiguous-case predictions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing Brain-Adapter outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL approaches on 3D acute intracranial pathology diagnosis.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of report text, extracted labels, and external validation across scanners and hospitals.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
